SELECT 
    op.order_id,
    op.payment_sequential,
    op.payment_type,
    op.payment_installments,
    op.payment_value,
    oi.price,
    oi.freight_value
FROM olist_order_payments op
JOIN olist_order_items oi ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE op.payment_sequential = 1
LIMIT 20

q6.sql:
SELECT 
    op.order_id,
    SUM(op.payment_value) as total_payments,
    SUM(oi.price) + SUM(oi.freight_value) as total_items_cost
FROM olist_order_payments op
JOIN olist_order_items oi ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY op.order_id
HAVING ABS(SUM(op.payment_value) - (SUM(oi.price) + SUM(oi.freight_value))) > 0.01
LIMIT 20

q7.sql:
SELECT 
    op.order_id,
    SUM(op.payment_value) as total_payments,
    SUM(oi.price) + SUM(oi.freight_value) as total_items_cost
FROM olist_order_payments op
JOIN olist_order_items oi ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY op.order_id
HAVING ABS(SUM(op.payment_value) - (SUM(oi.price) + SUM(oi.freight_value))) < 0.01
LIMIT 5

-- Check if review_creation_date is always at midnight (start of day) and what day of week it falls on
SELECT 
  COUNT(*) as total_rows,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(review_creation_date AS DATE)) as distinct_dates,
  MIN(CAST(review_creation_date AS DATE)) as min_date,
  MAX(CAST(review_creation_date AS DATE)) as max_date,
  -- Check if all times are 00:00:00
  COUNT(CASE WHEN review_creation_date LIKE '% 00:00:00' THEN 1 END) as midnight_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN review_creation_date NOT LIKE '% 00:00:00' THEN 1 END) as non_midnight_count
FROM olist_order_reviews

q1.sql:
-- Check the distribution of order statuses and their timestamps to understand the lifecycle
SELECT 
    order_status,
    COUNT(*) as count,
    MIN(order_purchase_timestamp) as earliest_purchase,
    MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) as latest_purchase,
    AVG(CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) as avg_purchase_time
FROM olist_orders
GROUP BY order_status
ORDER BY count DESC

q2.sql:
-- Check if order_estimated_delivery_date is always at midnight (end of day)
SELECT 
    DISTINCT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM CAST(order_estimated_delivery_date AS TIMESTAMP)) as hour,
    EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM CAST(order_estimated_delivery_date AS TIMESTAMP)) as minute,
    COUNT(*) as count
FROM olist_orders
GROUP BY hour, minute
ORDER BY count DESC

q3.sql:
-- Check the relationship between order_status and which timestamp columns are populated
-- For each status, check if approved_at, delivered_carrier_date, delivered_customer_date are null
SELECT

    COUNT(*) as total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_approved_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as null_approved,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as null_carrier,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as null_customer
FROM olist_orders
GROUP BY order_status
ORDER BY total DESC

-- Check if there are any orders where delivered_customer_date is before carrier_date (data quality issue)
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) as count,
    MIN(CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS TIMESTAMP) - CAST(order_delivered_carrier_date AS TIMESTAMP)) as min_diff,
    MAX(CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS TIMESTAMP) - CAST(order_delivered_carrier_date AS TIMESTAMP)) as max_diff
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL 
  AND order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS TIMESTAMP) < CAST(order_delivered_carrier_date AS TIMESTAMP)

q5.sql:
-- Check the relationship between order_purchase_timestamp and order_approved_at
-- How many orders have purchase timestamp before approval?
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) as total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP) < CAST(order_approved_at AS TIMESTAMP) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as purchase_before_approval,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP) > CAST(order_approved_at AS TIMESTAMP) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as purchase_after_approval,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP) = CAST(order_approved_at AS TIMESTAMP) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as same_time
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL

q6.sql:

    MIN(order_purchase_timestamp) as min_same,
    MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) as max_same
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND order_purchase_timestamp = order_approved_at

database_note: olist_orders is the central transaction table, linking customers via customer_id and items via order_id. olist_order_items records individual line items, connecting orders to products through product_id and sellers via seller_id. olist_order_payments and olist_order_reviews also join to olist_orders using order_id. olist_customers provides customer details, while olist_sellers holds seller information. olist_products describes items, and product_category_name_translation maps Portuguese category names to English. olist_geolocation offers location data for zip code prefixes, useful for joining with customer or seller addresses. olist_products_dataset is a redundant copy of olist_products and can be ignored. Use order_id to trace an order’s lifecycle, payments, reviews, and items.
